one_line: Nayaka-era minister, temple builder, and patron of learning in Kumbakonam and Thanjavur.

appearance.age_look: late 50s, slender but upright, with a composed scholarly bearing
appearance.face: oval face with medium-brown South Indian complexion, sharp nose, high forehead with a white vertical Shaivite tilak and small red dot, thin neatly trimmed grey mustache, fine lines at the eyes, default expression calm and thoughtful with a slight, kind smile
appearance.hair: long greying black hair tied into a low, neat bun at the back of the head, front hair smoothed back with no loose strands, topped by a simple off-white cotton shalya-style upper cloth wrapped once over the head like a light hood when outdoors but usually resting folded over one shoulder
appearance.costume: era-accurate late 16th–early 17th century South Indian Brahmin attire: a cream-coloured, ankle-length veshti/dhoti with a broad maroon border, tightly wrapped and pleated in front, worn high at the waist; upper body covered by a plain off-white cotton uttariya (shawl) draped over both shoulders and wrapped around the torso, leaving the chest modestly covered; beneath that, a pale sandalwood-beige long-sleeved angarkha-style tunic reaching mid-thigh with a simple round neck and side ties, made of fine cotton; bare feet in simple brown leather sandals; three strands of rudraksha and tulsi beads around the neck, a yajnopavita (sacred thread) indicated modestly across the left shoulder under the shawl, thin gold karnaphool earrings close to the earlobe, and a palm-leaf manuscript roll tucked into the belt-fold of the dhoti at his side as a subtle scholarly touch.
appearance.signature: a rolled palm-leaf manuscript bound with a red cotton cord in his right hand, with the end of the cord dangling and a simple wooden stylus tucked under the cord, held like a precious working document of governance and learning rather than a weapon.

ref_desc: Govinda Dikshita is a late-50s South Indian scholar-minister with greying hair in a low bun, oval calm face with Shaivite tilak, cream dhoti with maroon border, beige tunic, off-white shawl, simple beads and sandals, holding a red-tied palm-leaf manuscript.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Govinda Dikshita standing in a neutral pose: a dignified late-50s South Indian scholar-minister with a medium-brown complexion, oval thoughtful face, sharp nose, thin grey mustache, high forehead marked by a white vertical Shaivite tilak with a small red dot, and calm, kind eyes. His hair is black greying, smoothed back and tied in a low bun at the back of his head, with a simple off-white cotton shawl that can be wrapped as a hood but here rests folded over his left shoulder. He wears an era-accurate cream ankle-length veshti/dhoti with a broad maroon border, neatly pleated in front, secured high at the waist, over simple brown leather sandals. His upper body is fully covered by a pale sandalwood-beige long-sleeved angarkha-style cotton tunic reaching mid-thigh, and an off-white cotton uttariya shawl draped over both shoulders and wrapped across the torso so the chest is modestly covered. Show three strands of rudraksha and tulsi beads around his neck, a hint of the sacred thread under the shawl, and small plain gold earrings at the lobes. In his right hand he holds his signature prop: a rolled palm-leaf manuscript bound with a red cotton cord, with a slender wooden stylus tucked under the cord, presented as the central symbol of his temple-building, educational, and administrative work. Use a restrained palette of cream, maroon, off-white, sandalwood beige, and brown, and ensure the design looks consistently redrawable in an all-ages, historically grounded South Indian Nayaka-period style.
